We compare language-based methods (LangSplat [39],Occam’s LGS [9], Dr.Splat [18]), instance-feature-based methods (OpenGaussian [48], InstanceGaussian [29], COS3D [54] LaGa [6]), and a point-based method (THGS [12]). PairGS-Fast denotes our fast version, which utilizes center-based lifting [9] for feature initialization (Sec. 3.2). The two versions differ only in this initialization method. The high-fidelity version (unmarked) is our default. Accurate is measured by mAcc@0.50.

Figure 5. Qualitative comparison. We visualize open-vocabulary object selection results on LERF [21] dataset. Compared to languagebased [18] and instance-feature-based [6, 29, 48] baselines, PairGS produces cleaner 3D Gaussian segmentations for objects in contact with others, such as a spoon or a spatula. It also yields coherent instance separation for larger objects. In particular, THGS [12] is point-based and considers only Gaussian centers, which often leads to noisy Gaussians in contact regions and along object boundaries.
Table 2. Semantic segmentation results on ScanNet [11] dataset.

Figure 2. Overview of PairGS. Our method begins with a pretrained 3DGS [19] and initializes its features by lifting SAM [22] masked CLIP [41] features from each view. Using semantic descriptors and positional cues, we construct low-dimensional node descriptors to propose sparse edge candidates. Precise pairwise affinities are then computed only on these candidates to build the relation graph efficiently. Finally, our TreeDBSCAN algorithm builds the hierarchical cluster tree.

Figure 6. Qualitative comparison. We visualize open-vocabulary semantic segmentation on ScanNet [11] dataset. Our method demonstrates robust performance across diverse queries, accurately segmenting objects at varying scales, such as large desks and smaller chairs.
